gaps: F2 (intermittent ack-paced stall) is confirmed as a behavior but its mechanism was not isolated: it did not reproduce in the two targeted isolation runs (10/10 and 3/3 healthy), so no root cause is asserted.

The acceptance criteria used here are the two customer requirements relayed in the requesting thread (input dispatched immediately during frame delivery; drop stale frames and send only the newest at a configurable rate). Requirement fit was assessed as Standards review, not Spec review.

findings.claim: The shipped default does not satisfy the customer's stale-frame requirement. Latest-frame-wins is enforced only above the socket, so in the default push pacing a client that falls behind still drains a stale backlog. The requirement is met only when the client opts into ack pacing, which the default does not do.
findings.evidence: Release binary at HEAD against real Chrome, 4s reader stall, ~58 fps source. Push (default): 59 frames arrived in the first 300ms after resume, 40 of them measurably older than 1.5s, 2374 KB drained, oldest delivered frame 4003ms stale. Ack pacing via ?pacing=ack under the identical stall: exactly 1 stale frame. Independently reproduces the branch's own measurement.
findings.layer: end-to-end delivery path, transport hop below the application channel

findings.claim: Ack-paced delivery, the only mode that satisfies the requirement, is not reliable. An ack-paced connection intermittently delivers zero or one frame and never recovers, and it degrades severely under sustained input on the same connection. Push is unaffected in every trial. The failure mode is a permanently blank or frozen preview, which is the outcome the change's own rationale gives for preferring push.
findings.evidence: Total stall observed on ~6 of ~35 ack connections across five independently written harnesses (0 frames in 3.5s with socket open and zero acks; 0 frames in 4s on a cold start; 1 frame in 2.5s), and never on ~20 push connections. Degradation under input on the same socket: ack delivered 3.7 fps at 200 input/s and 10.3 fps at 250 input/s against 60 fps idle, while push held 62.6-62.7 fps at every rate from 30 to 250 (6/6). Client-side write ordering excluded: the client's own socket write backlog measured 0 bytes in all four runs, so the acks left the client promptly and the delay is server-side. Mechanism not isolated: it did not reproduce in 10/10 or 3/3 targeted isolation runs, so no root cause is asserted.
findings.layer: end-to-end per-connection delivery under concurrent client traffic

findings.claim: Keyboard input, half of the customer's first requirement, does not work in the shape this change documents. dispatch_input forwards parsed.get("code") and parsed.get("text") straight into the CDP payload, so an absent field is sent as JSON null, Chrome rejects the whole command, and the error is discarded by `let _ =`. Every keyUp is dropped, and every non-printable key is dropped in both directions.
findings.evidence: Against real Chrome: the shape documented in README, docs/src/app/streaming/page.mdx and the new skill-data/core/references/streaming.md ({key, text}, no code) produced keys=[] at the DOM; adding code produced keys=[xyz]; {key, code} without text produced keys=[] again. Direct CDP probe returns -32602 'Failed to deserialize params.code - BINDINGS: string value expected' and the same for params.text. Replaying the dashboard's exact payload from packages/dashboard/src/components/viewport.tsx, which sets text: undefined for every keyUp and for every KEY_INFO entry without a text field (Escape, ArrowLeft/Up/Right/Down, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown), yielded keydown=["q"] keyup=[] : arrows and Escape never arrived and no keyup ever arrived.
findings.layer: end-to-end input dispatch, CDP parameter contract
findings.path: gate.sh siblings input_keyboard -> packages/dashboard/src/components/viewport.tsx; corroborated by map depth-1 impact on packages/dashboard/src/types.ts#StreamMessage

findings.claim: Under ack pacing the writer reparses the entire frame message as JSON on every send purely to read seq, including the base64 image payload, when the value is already known at construction time.
findings.evidence: frame_seq_of does serde_json::from_str::<Value>(frame) on the whole message. Measured frame size ~40 KB (2374 KB over 59 frames), so at the observed ~60 fps this is roughly 2.4 MB/s of JSON parsing on the ack path, which is the path the customer must use. Avoidable by carrying seq beside the string in the watch channel.
findings.layer: per-frame hot path under ack pacing

findings.claim: Adding required `seq` to the dashboard's FrameMessage interface breaks the dashboard TypeScript build, the failure mode recorded in the Rust-only prepush case.
findings.evidence: Refuted at the claim's layer (type checking, not reasoning): FrameMessage is referenced in exactly two places, its own declaration and the StreamMessage union in packages/dashboard/src/types.ts. Nothing in the repo constructs a FrameMessage, so a new required field is only ever narrowed, never supplied. CI builds the dashboard via next build on both ci.yml and release.yml.

findings.claim: Moving idle_activity.mark() inside the client_slot guard lets an actively driven preview idle out, regressing the 1h idle timeout merged from main in #1605.
findings.evidence: Refuted on reachability at the claim's own layer: input only fails to mark activity while client_slot is None, which is the window where no CDP client is attached (browser relaunch). Starving the timer requires that window to cover the full 1h idle period with input arriving only inside it. No such state was reachable in ~35 connections and 12 churn cycles; the session never idled out and the page never reset.

findings.claim: The rewritten connect/teardown path regresses #1476, where a stream client disconnect intermittently reset the session's active page to about:blank.
findings.evidence: Refuted empirically at the end-to-end layer: 12 abrupt socket destroys (not WS close frames) across push, ?pacing=ack, and ?maxFps=5, including a disconnect while the writer was mid-flight, left get url at https://example.com/, the injected DOM node alive (animation counter still advancing), and the stream still enabled. Bounded claim: #1476 is reported as intermittent, so 12 cycles is absence of observed regression, not proof of absence.

findings.claim: A high ack banked before the opening frame is written wedges the connection, because the seed-frame path sets awaiting_ack without settling it against the already-banked watermark the way the writer loop does.
findings.evidence: Refuted by reading the channel contract at the layer of the claim: ack_rx is created from watch::channel(0) before the reader is spawned, so any send_if_modified from a premature ack bumps the version the writer has not yet observed, and ack_rx.changed() therefore resolves immediately on the first select pass and clears awaiting_ack. The branch's own test_ack_ahead_of_the_stream_does_not_wedge_the_writer covers the config-message variant. Note this refutation does not cover F2, which is a different and unexplained stall.

findings.claim: The WebSocket origin allowlist admits only localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and file://, so the customer's stated topology (agent-browser in a sandbox, interactive preview rendered in the end user's browser) cannot connect a browser client directly and must proxy. Ack pacing then bounds only the daemon-to-proxy hop, leaving the proxy-to-browser hop with the buffering the change exists to remove, and nothing in the new documentation says so.
findings.evidence: Verified against the running server: Origin absent -> accepted, http://localhost:3000 -> accepted, https://app.example.com -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden. is_allowed_origin at cli/src/native/stream/mod.rs:499 is untouched by this diff.
findings.layer: deployment topology and documented guarantee scope

findings.claim: EXTERNAL (ctate). stream disable returns while a slow client's input reader is still active. shutdown() awaits only accept_task and cdp_task; the per-client tasks are detached, and reader_task.abort() runs only if the writer reaches the select! shutdown arm, which a writer blocked in ws_tx.send() never does.
findings.evidence: Confirmed by reading at the layer of the claim: mod.rs:209-218 awaits accept_task and cdp_task only; websocket.rs aborts the reader after the select loop, and the shutdown arm is inside that loop. Reachability of the blocked-writer state is not theoretical, this gate created it deliberately to verify input priority. The exploitable consequence did NOT reproduce: 7 clicks written after 'Streaming disabled' returned produced 0 DOM mousedown events, apparently because tearing down cdp_task renders the stream's CdpClient unusable, so today the protection is incidental rather than enforced. Reasoned, not observed: idle_activity.mark() now sits inside the client_slot guard and the slot still holds a live Arc<CdpClient>, so a leaked reader can keep marking daemon activity after disable and hold the #1605 idle timeout open indefinitely.

findings.claim: EXTERNAL (ctate). Initial maxFps accounting is wrong in both directions. next_allowed and last_sent are stamped Instant::now() at connect regardless of whether the seed frame was actually sent, so a cached frame is not charged against the cap and a second frame follows immediately, while with no cache the phantom last_sent delays the first real frame by a full interval.
findings.evidence: Measured against the release binary at HEAD. Cache present: maxFps=2 delivered gaps of 8ms then 502/501/501/502ms, and maxFps=1 delivered 10ms then 1002/1002ms, so exactly one frame escapes the cap at connect. No cache, cap arriving by config message: first frame at 1002ms under maxFps=1 although nothing had ever been sent on that connection. Both halves share one root cause, the unconditional initialization at websocket.rs after the seed-frame block.
findings.layer: per-connection throttle accounting at connection setup

findings.claim: broadcast_frame is public with zero production call sites and emits a frame carrying no seq, which silently disables ack pacing for that frame because frame_seq_of returns None and the writer declines to hold. This is the unguarded-primitive-left-reachable shape already recorded in this repo's gate-miss ledger.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep: the only callers are the new tests in cli/src/native/stream/mod.rs. The branch's own test_frame_seq_of_reads_the_id_the_client_acks documents the None case as leaving the writer unblocked, so the degradation is by design for a seq-less frame; the hazard is that the public entry point producing seq-less frames remains available to the next caller.
